Meetings are broadcast live on Glendale TV, viewable on Spectrum Cable, channel 6, and AT&T U-
verse, channel 99. Meetings are also streamed live in high definition (HD) on the city's webpage,
glendaleca.gov/live, on YouTube.com/myglendale, and on Apple TV, Roku, and Amazon Fire
devices using a free app called Screenweave and choosing “Glendale TV” from the menu. Meetings
are also archived on the City Website for viewing anytime at glendaleca.gov/agendas. Call (818)
548-4013 for program schedules. For public comments and questions during the meeting, call (818)
937-8100. Public comments on a specific agenda item will be taken when that agenda item is
discussed. If you have any question about matters on the agenda, or requests for assistance,
please contact the City Clerk at (818) 548-2090 during regular business hours.
  PLEASE TURN OFF CELLULAR PHONES WHILE INSIDE THE MEETING LOCATION
In compliance with the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) of 1990, auxiliary hearing aids, sign
language translation, and Braille transcripts are available upon request. Assisted listening devices
are available same-day upon request. At least 48 hours (or two business days) notice is required for
requests regarding sign language translation and Braille transcription services. All documents
related to open session items on this agenda that are received less than 72 hours prior to this
meeting, and are public records, will be available for review in the Office of the City Clerk, 613 E.
Broadway, RM 110, Glendale, CA 91206.
Translation services are provided for meetings through the use of bilingual staff for speakers who
wish to utilize the service as available. Speakers should state their request by contacting the City
Clerk’s office at (818) 548-2090, at least 24 hours prior to the scheduled meeting. Please specify
the language for which you require translation. The exclusive use of City provided interpreters is not
required and persons are welcome to use their own interpreter or speak in their native language.

5. CITY COUNCIL/STAFF COMMENTS
  Councilmember Devine stated she, and Mayor Brotman attended the 10th Anniversary of
  Comfort Women Peace Monument. She also thanked the police department and the
  community for a successful National Night Out. She congratulated Glendale Arts on their 15th
  anniversary. She also mentioned that the Museum of Martial Arts will be opening in October
  here in Glendale. Devine stated there is an opening on the Historic Preservation Commission
  and she encouraged those who are interested to apply. Also, Councilmember Devine
  requested to adjourn the meeting in the memory of Sebastian Sonny Sardo.

  Councilmember Kassakhian stated most Councilmembers and the City Manager attended the
  Independent Cities Association Conference in the City of Coronado to discuss issues facing
  cities.

  Councilmember Najarian also commented on the passing of Sebastian Sonny Sardo. He
  asked his colleagues to support a review of the Downtown Noise Overlay Zone considering
  future uses of businesses on Central Ave. and Brand Blvd. He requested a report to evaluate
  the current situation and how it would impact future development.

  Mayor Brotman stated he and councilmember Asatryan conducted the first interview panel for
  the Civil Service Commission and they would like to nominate Armineh Megrabyan. Mayor
  Brotman stated that he would like to discuss a shared mobility pilot program for the next
  business agenda. He mentioned that Council has previously debated this topic and had RFPs
  in the past. Mayor Brotman stated that he attended National Night Out and managed to attend
  seven locations.

  3
   City Manager Golanian stated that the city has embarked on the 2024 Integrated Resource
  Plan and that the city had two town hall meetings. He mentions the IRP outlines Glendale’s
  energy needs and the resources the city can use for the next 20 years. He encouraged
  community members to attend the 3rd town hall meeting on August 12th. He invited Elizabeth
  Harris to discuss the first clothing swap event scheduled on August 12th. Harris mentioned that
  this event will give the public the opportunity to swap clothes, reduce waste and receive a new
  wardrobe in return.

  Councilmember Najarian recognized and welcomed the special guests in the audience from
  the IBEW Local 18.
